minutes.headline: Sewer Commission voted to send residents a gravity-only sewer extension proposal for Upland/Eastern and White/Maple Parkway.
minutes.summary: The commission heard its engineers compare gravity and low-pressure sewer options for two neighborhoods and chose to present only the gravity option, as one combined project, to residents. It also discussed ARPA uses and infiltration from old clay pipes, a 7 Mass Ave housing project's sewer review, the Pond View Commons 40B decision, and the FY22 budget status.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted by roll call to present a gravity-only sewer extension to residents as one combined project and to send a solicitation to the streets.
The proposal covers the Upland/Eastern and White/Maple Parkway neighborhoods, with a 20-year betterment and more detail available on request.
On the 7 Mass Ave housing project, the applicant is to submit updated plans for peer review by the planning board's engineer, aiming to return in about 30 days.
The commission asked the new DPW director to set up a meeting on infiltration and ARPA uses with the engineers and Leominster counterparts.
The business manager sought approval to pay the second invoice completing the engineering memo contract; the minutes list the item under votes.

why_it_matters: Homes on the affected streets may be asked to take on a sewer betterment spread over 20 years, and the low-pressure option was set aside partly because it shifts pump purchase, installation and maintenance onto owners.
The 7 Mass Ave housing project's sewer capacity and flow are under review, and ARPA money for pump stations or pipe lining could affect what sewer users and taxpayers fund later.
watch_next: The solicitation to the affected streets, and any resident vote or betterment decision that follows it.
The 7 Mass Ave applicant's updated plans and peer review, with a return to the agenda targeted within about 30 days.
